h3: Late Fee Waiver entries
p: A Late Fee Waiver entry with Late Fee Payment allocation type and No Cash status debits account 404007 and credits account 112603.
When the Reversal Indicator is Y, the entry posts as follows:

ul.li: With Late Fee Payment allocation type, No Cash status, and Reversal Indicator Y, the entry debits account 404007 and credits account 404008.
With Late Fee Payment allocation type, No Cash status, Reversal Indicator Y, and Charged off Flag Y, the entry debits account 404008 and credits account 404007.

h3: NSF Fee Waiver entries
p: An NSF Fee Waiver entry with NSF Fee Payment allocation type and No Cash status debits account 404007 and credits account 112603.
When Reversal Indicator Y applies, the entry depends on the charged off flag:

ul.li: With Charged off Flag Y, the entry debits account 112603 and credits account 404007.
Without Charged off Flag Y, the entry debits account 404007 and credits account 404008.

h3: Auto Payment Cash in charged-off entries
p: Auto Payment Cash in charged-off entries apply when an auto payment is received on a charged-off loan. The debit and credit accounts depend on the repayment allocation type. All allocation types debit account 145023; most credit account 744008, while Unallocated Credit credits account 245000.
h3: Auto Payment Cash Out reversal entries
p: Auto Payment Cash Out reversal entries apply when an Auto Payment reversal has Cash Out status. The debit and credit accounts depend on the repayment allocation type. The system credits account 145023 for every reversal entry listed here. The debit account is 112603 for interest, late fee, NSF fee and snooze fee allocations, 112601 for principal allocations, and 245000 for unallocated credit allocations.
h3: Auto Payment Cash Out charged-off reversal entries
p: Auto Payment Cash Out charged-off reversal entries apply when an Auto Payment has Cash Out status, reversal indicator Y, and charged off flag Y. The debit and credit accounts depend on the repayment allocation type.
Snooze Fee Payment entries use Cash in status rather than Cash Out status.
h3: Scheduled Payment Cash in entries
p: Scheduled Payment Cash in entries record the accounting effect when a scheduled payment is received, with the debit and credit accounts depending on the allocation type.
h3: Scheduled Payment Cash in charged-off entries
Scheduled Payment Cash Out reversal entries
p: Scheduled Payment Cash Out reversal entries apply when a scheduled payment has Cash Out status and Reversal Indicator Y. The debit account depends on the allocation type, while the credit account stays the same.
Apply Fee Return with Late Fee Payment allocation type and No Cash status has no accounting entries, whether or not Reversal Indicator Y is set.
A Loan Disbursement Principal Cash Out entry debits account 112601 and credits account 145023 with status pass, mapping Loan portfolio to Fund source.
h3: Verified Transaction Refund/Provisional Credit Cash in entries
p: A Verified Transaction Refund/Provisional Credit Cash in entry posts to account 145023 as a debit and credits the receiving account with status pass, mapping the fund source to the relevant receivable, liability, or loan portfolio account.
h3: Verified Transaction Refund/Provisional Credit Cash in reversal entries
p: A Transaction Refund/Provisional Credit Cash in entry with the Y flag debits account 145023 and credits an income or expense account based on the payment type, with the Fund source mapped to the corresponding charge-off income or expense account.
h3: Verified Transaction Refund/Provisional Credit Cash Out reversal entries
p: A Verified Transaction Refund/Provisional Credit Cash Out entry reverses a cash-out payment by debiting a cash account and crediting the fund source account. The entry applies when the Y flag is set and carries a pass status.

h3: Worked examples
p: A fraudulent loan with a principal of 1,000 has overdue amounts of 100.00 interest, 50.00 fees, and 30.00 penalties. An operations user verifies the charge-off entries before posting them. The figures are illustrative. The example shows how interest, fees, and penalties split into different debit and credit accounts during a fraud charge-off.

A non-fraud loan with a principal of 1,000 carries 40.00 in overdue fees and 20.00 in overdue penalties. A product administrator verifies the charge-off entries for both portions. The fee portion credits Fee Receivable while the penalty portion credits Penalty Receivable.

A recovered payment of 80.00 includes 60.00 in fees and 20.00 in penalties. An operations user posts the OCA repayment entries and checks the debit and credit accounts. Both portions debit Other receivables and credit recoveries, so changing the portion type does not change the accounts.

A loan disbursement of 1,000 uses the Principal allocation type and Cash Out status. A loan officer verifies that the entry debits Loans Receivable and credits the Suspense/Clearing account. The entry moves the disbursed principal from the clearing account to the loan portfolio.
